motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Clips swap to stills, result animations and switch transition off, landing reveals and smooth scroll off.

translator.rules: Carton ground, unframed white instruction panel at 440px, framed Translation Facts panel, verdict plate, round trip, checks, print slip.

landing.rules: The sentence is the layout: full-bleed single-colour section fields, 12-column grid, five clamp type steps, fixed bar that takes the field's ink, scroll reveals, carton render rotated -4deg, cropped 26vw name in the close. Uses no frames or bars, and no alert red in CSS.

video.rules: Same palette and face; frames 8px and bars 14-18px at 1920 wide.

3d.rules: Cycles, Standard view transform for exact carton blue, one soft key-light shadow, transparent background for the carton.

narrative.overview:
Every surface borrows the grammar of the FDA Drug Facts label the instructions come from: a field of carton blue, white panels drawn in black, heavy section bars, thin rules, and one plain federal grotesque. The tool's answer is set as a "Translation Facts" panel, so the result reads like the label it was checked against rather than like a software card. Structure is drawn in ink, not implied with shadows or tinted cards.

The working screen is dense and literal: two columns on the blue ground, the instruction form on the left, the framed facts panel on the right, read top to bottom from verdict to translation to round trip to checks. The landing page uses the same palette and type at poster scale, one field of colour per section, and lets the sentences carry the layout.

Colour is quarantined. Carton blue owns the ground and the bar; white owns the work; ink owns every word and every line; alert red appears only where a check failed. Motion exists to give feedback and to show the round trip, never to decorate.
keyCharacteristics: Carton-blue shell, white working panels, black ink structure.
One framed panel with 10px black section bars and 2px rules, after the Drug Facts label.
Alert red only on failed checks, struck words and the "check this" verdict plate.
Public Sans alone, 900/800/600/400, with a Chinese fallback.
State always given as a word plus a form, never hue alone.

rules.name: The Carton Owns the Ground Rule
rules.body: Blue is a field, never a component colour inside a panel. Inside white panels, everything is ink.

rules.name: The Quarantined Red Rule
rules.body: Alert red marks a failed check, a struck word or the "check this" verdict plate. Errors in the form, the "too long" refusal and every other state use ink and weight, not red.

rules.name: The Word and Form Rule
rules.body: Every state is named in words and drawn as a form: "Failed" in a 2px red box, struck versus underlined words with a key underneath, a verdict plate with a sentence. Colour only reinforces.

rules.name: The One Grotesque Rule
rules.body: Public Sans is the only face on every surface, in the HyperFrames clips and in the explainer. No second family, no mono, no serif.

rules.name: The Translation Leads Rule
rules.body: In any panel or print that carries a translation, the translation is the largest text after the panel title (30px on screen, 26pt on the printed slip).

rules.name: The Printed Label Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat like printed card stock. Separate with ink lines and fields of colour, never with shadows, blur or tonal elevation.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: Nothing is rounded. Not buttons, not inputs, not the switch knob, not video frames.

dos: Do set the shell on carton blue and the work on white, with all structure in ink (3px frame, 10px bars, 2px rules).
Do keep alert red to failed checks, struck words and the "check this" verdict plate.
Do name every state in words and draw it as a form, so it reads without colour.
Do use Public Sans alone, keeping the Noto Sans SC / YaHei / PingFang fallback on any surface that shows a translation.
Do keep every corner square and every surface flat.

Do limit motion on the working screen to feedback (press, focus, switch, timer), the two HyperFrames clips with their still fallbacks, and the result's verdict stamp plus the strike/underline draw; turn all of it off under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

Do write the positive verdict as "No problems found by the automatic checks" and carry "Prototype – not medical advice" on every surface (the translator bar, the printed slip, the landing footer, the explainer end card).
donts: Don't call a translation "safe" anywhere: in copy, verdicts, the slip, video or alt text (the product name and the "Safer mode" control are the only uses of the word, and neither describes a translation).
Don't use red for form errors, the "too long" refusal, hover states or emphasis.
Don't add shadows, rounded corners, gradients or tinted cards on grey.
Don't add a second typeface beyond the Chinese fallback.
Don't let a clip's text render below 14px; swap in the still instead.
Don't present the illustrated flip ("ít hơn" / "less") as real model output; label it as an illustration.
